LESSON: WRITING 2.4.1 PRE-WRITING

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.4: Writing 2.4.1 Pre-writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 2.4.1 Pre-writing, part of Strand 2 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade one ENGLISH LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: how to 1. How do we sit when writing? 2. How do we position writing materials when writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

N. • demonstrate tactile- kinaesthetic perception in preparation for braille touch writing (for learners with blindnes

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 2.4.1 Pre-writing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

S. , • value the importance of positioning oneself and writing materials appropriately in preparation for writing. • Learners to listen audio visual clips on sitting posture and discuss with peers. • Learners with low vision are guided to observe at each other’s sitting posture and identify the correct posture for writing. Learners with blindness be given one on one description of sitting posture to identify the correct posture for writing. • In pairs, learners are guide to demonstrate and practise the correct body posture for writing. • Learners are guided to individually identify writing materials that are correctly positioned. • Learners are guided to individually demonstrate and practise positioning writing materials appropriately. • Learners are guided to individually write from the left to the right. • In pairs, guide learners to role play how to 1. How do we sit when writing? 2. How do we position writing materials when writing? 31 use their exercise Books/braille papers well.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 2.4.1 Pre-writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Creativity and imagination: A learner role plays how to use their exercise Books/braille papers well.

Values:
• Unity is enhanced as the learner displays team spirit as they work together during pair and group activities.

• Love is enhanced as the learner shares with peers drawing and colouring materials.

Pertinent Contemporary Issues:

Life skills (self-esteem) learners acquire an enhanced level of self- esteem as they learn how to sit appropriately in preparation for writing.

Links to other Learning Areas:
Correct body posture while writing is emphasised in Kiswahili Language Activities.

Suggested learning resources

• String beads,

• Thread,

• Small and big objects with different textures for sorting

• Crayon, drawing books

• Textbooks in braille and in appropriate font and colour contrast
